about_hero_subtitle: Building technology-driven solutions for early health risk awareness.
mission_text1: SwasthSathi exists to bridge the gap between rural communities and early health awareness. In India, millions of people discover chronic conditions like diabetes and hypertension only after symptoms become severe—often too late for preventive care.
mission_text2: We believe that early screening should be accessible to everyone, regardless of location, literacy, or economic status. Our platform is designed to support timely medical consultation, not replace it.
problem_late_desc: Most chronic diseases are detected only after complications arise, when treatment becomes costly and complex.
problem_awareness_desc: Early symptoms of diabetes and hypertension often go unnoticed, especially in rural areas with limited health education.
problem_access_desc: Rural India faces challenges like distance to clinics, lack of transport, and shortage of healthcare workers.
problem_overcrowded_desc: Public hospitals are overwhelmed with patients, leaving little time for preventive care and early screening.
team_subtitle: A collaborative, interdisciplinary team of four tech enthusiasts united by a shared vision: making healthcare accessible through responsible technology.
ethics_not_diagnostic_desc: SwasthSathi is a screening platform, not a medical diagnosis system.
ethics_awareness_desc: We empower users with early risk awareness to seek timely medical consultation.
ethics_professional_desc: Final medical decisions must always be taken by certified healthcare professionals.
ethics_footer: We are committed to using technology responsibly, transparently, and ethically in healthcare.

factor_age_context: Risk of diabetes and hypertension increases with age. NFHS-5 data shows a 14× higher odds ratio for those above 50 years.
factor_obesity_context: BMI ≥30 is associated with 12× higher diabetes risk. Excess body fat increases insulin resistance and blood pressure.
factor_overweight_context: For South Asians, health risks begin at BMI ≥23 — lower than the global threshold of 25. Even modest weight reduction improves outcomes.
factor_abdominal_obesity_context: Waist circumference >90 cm (men) or >80 cm (women) indicates visceral fat — a key driver of insulin resistance and elevated blood pressure.
factor_blood_sugar_high_context: Fasting blood sugar ≥126 mg/dL meets the ADA diagnostic criterion for diabetes. Clinical confirmation and consultation are essential.
factor_blood_sugar_prediabetes_context: Fasting blood sugar 100–125 mg/dL is the pre-diabetes range. Lifestyle changes at this stage can prevent progression to full diabetes.
factor_blood_pressure_context: Elevated blood pressure damages blood vessels over time. JNC-8 guidelines define hypertension as BP ≥140/90 mmHg.
factor_diagnosed_diabetes_context: A prior diabetes diagnosis significantly elevates combined metabolic risk, especially alongside hypertension (60.5% co-occurrence rate, NFHS-5).
factor_diagnosed_hypertension_context: Existing hypertension raises the risk of cardiovascular complications. Regular monitoring and adherence to prescribed treatment are critical.
factor_diabetes_symptoms_context: Symptoms like frequent urination, excessive thirst, and unexplained fatigue cluster together in early-stage diabetes and should not be ignored.
factor_htn_symptoms_context: Persistent headaches, dizziness, and palpitations may indicate elevated blood pressure. A BP reading should be taken promptly.
factor_family_history_context: Having a first-degree relative with diabetes or hypertension raises your own risk by 2–3× due to shared genetic and lifestyle factors.
factor_sedentary_context: Physical inactivity reduces insulin sensitivity and raises blood pressure. Even 30 minutes of walking daily significantly lowers metabolic risk.
factor_diet_context: High-fat, high-sugar, and high-salt diets drive weight gain, insulin resistance, and elevated BP — the three pillars of metabolic syndrome.
factor_smoking_context: Smoking directly damages blood vessel walls, raising blood pressure and increasing insulin resistance. Risk drops significantly within months of quitting.
factor_alcohol_context: Regular alcohol intake raises blood pressure, adds empty calories, and disrupts glucose metabolism — contributing to both diabetes and hypertension risk.
